transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-09-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Alyssa Chen (Portside Head of ML), Mark Rivera (Portside CTO), Sam Ortiz (Portside Infra)

Summary:
Portside is evaluating options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for a customer-facing NLP feature that will touch payment metadata (so there are PCI/residency concerns). Primary driver is keeping per-token unit economics low while meeting a 200ms SLO for 95th percentile on their prioritised path. Budget is limited; they want a pilot to validate unit costs and latency. They asked about batching windows, prefix/KV caching, quantized model variants, and fallback routing. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching and cache levers, dedicated vs hosted capacity, private/VPC concerns (PCI), pilot scope and metrics, security docs and SSO/KMS.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alyssa: Hey Jordan, hi Priya. Doing good, thanks. Busy week here at Portside.
[00:09] Mark: Yep, thanks for doing this, we've got a few people with questions.
[00:12] Jordan: Great — quick round table, then we'll jump to the costing stuff. Priya, anything to add?
[00:16] Priya: I'll mostly cover the latency/cost tradeoffs and the benchmark plan. I'll also take notes on the prompt set you share.
[00:22] Alyssa: Cool. Background: we're a retail checkout platform, Portside, we run recommendation/assistant features across web and mobile. We're planning to add a conversational order assistant that touches payment references — non-PII but still within PCI cardholder environment which complicates residency. Our goals are 200ms p95 for main path and keep monthly inference spend under USD 12k for pilot.
[00:39] Jordan: Got it. So main questions are: how do Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private affect per-token costs, and what levers do we have (batching, prefix caching, quantization) to hit that budget without blowing latency SLOs?
[00:52] Mark: Yes. Also interested in fallback policies if the dedicated pool is saturated during peak. We want predictable billing.

[00:58] Priya: Okay, quick overview. Hosted is easiest to start: pay per token, no infra to manage, but unit price is higher because we're absorbing capacity risk. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with lower per-token price and predictable throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strong residency or compliance needs but comes with ops and fixed costs. On levers: batching increases throughput and reduces per-token compute overhead but adds latency. Prefix/KV cache — if you have repeated prompts or a lot of shared history — can cut token compute significantly. Quantized model variants (4-bit, int8-ish) reduce GPU memory and cost but may slightly affect quality.
[01:28] Alyssa: When you say batching adds latency, what are we talking about? Average batch windows? We have web requests so can't add much tail.
[01:34] Priya: Right. For web interactive features we recommend tiny batch windows — 5-20ms ideal — with continuous batching. You'll still see some savings because batching amortizes the kernel overhead across tokens. In our benchmarks a 10ms batching window with 64 concurrent micros had about 8-12% token-cost drop, p95 latency impact was about +5-15ms depending on model size. Those numbers vary with prompt length and concurrency.
[02:02] Sam: That 10ms window sounds small, is that real? How does it work on our side?
[02:05] Priya: It's part of Redwood's runtime — continuous batching where the runtime groups arriving requests over a short window. On dedicated pools you can also tune batching policies aggressively because you control throughput. Hosted has heuristics to avoid harming p95.
[02:16] Mark: How does KV cache help? We have a lot of templated prompts for product info, so maybe reuse.
[02:20] Priya: KV cache avoids re-computing past layers for repeated prefixes. If your assistant often uses the same system prompt and product detail blocks, hits to KV cache reduce compute per request dramatically. In practice, customers saw 30-60% token compute reduction on highly repetitive flows. The trick is your repetition rate — we can estimate once we see sample prompt histograms.
[02:41] Alyssa: We'll share a sample of production prompts — anonymized. Can you estimate the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for, say, 500k tokens / month before caching?
[02:50] Jordan: Sure, roughly — hosted might be around $x per 1k tokens and dedicated's effective unit with reserved capacity can be roughly 30-50% lower depending on utilization. I'll confirm numbers in the pricing sheet.
[03:02] Mark: Important: our finance wants a burn predictability to fit the USD 12k pilot cap. If dedicated needs committed monthly spend, can it be sized small?
[03:10] Jordan: Dedicated can be configured with smaller pools plus burst; you commit to baseline and get discounts. If you're not sure on utilization, a hybrid pilot often works: start Hosted with routing rules and then move predictable traffic to Dedicated as you understand utilization.
[03:22] Sam: For PCI/residency — if payment references are in requests we may need Private or at least VPC-hosted control plane. How strict is Redwood's Hosted option on residency?
[03:30] Priya: Hosted is multi-tenant and we can't guarantee air-gapped handling; we do have SOC 2 controls, encrypted at rest, and region controls, but for strict PCI you'll likely need Dedicated in a VPC or Private with customer-managed networking. We can run a security review.
[03:44] Alyssa: We probably need at least VPC with logs forwarded to our SIEM, KMS integration and SSO. Does Redwood support bring-your-own-key?
[03:50] Jordan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support KMS integrations and BYOK workflows. Hosted supports server-side keys managed by Redwood but we can discuss HSM integrations under enterprise contracts.
[03:59] Mark: Ok that helps. Back to unit economics: what are the main knobs you tune to reduce cost per useful token?
[04:06] Priya: Four main knobs: batching window, model quantization (and smaller models), caching/prefix reuse, and routing to cheaper model variants for lower-criticality paths. Also token trimming in prompts and early stopping heuristics. We can pair those with tooling in Redwood Optimize where we surface recommendations.
[04:22] Alyssa: We have constrained dev time; can you recommend a minimal pilot that proves both latency and unit cost?
[04:27] Priya: Yes. Minimal pilot: 1) Portside shares 2 weeks of prompts; 2) Redwood runs a small benchmark on 3 candidate model variants (full, quantized, smaller) measuring p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens; 3) We'll run a caching simulation to estimate KV hit rate savings; 4) 2-week live pilot on Hosted with routing rules and throttles, or on a small Dedicated pool if residency requires. That should fit your USD 12k if we scope the live traffic cap.
[04:55] Jordan: We'll also give a pricing sheet that maps committed capacity to effective per-token rates.
[04:59] Mark: Are there tooling or code changes we need for prefix caching?
[05:02] Priya: Minimal changes: you need to send a cache key or structured inputs so the runtime can identify prefixes and hit the cache. Alternatively, Redwood's SDK has helpers to autogenerate cache keys if you pass the same system messages. We can share the SDK snippet.
[05:16] Alyssa: Quality — if we quantize to 4-bit or run a smaller model for some fallbacks, what's the quality delta? Our assistants are user-facing so small regressions may be noticeable.
[05:25] Priya: We'll run evaluation on your prompt set. Historically, 4-bit quantization on certain LLM families has negligible quality regression for instruction-following in many cases, but it's model dependent. Smaller models trade more quality. That's why the benchmark with A/B evals on your prompts is critical.
[05:39] Sam: For peak traffic, if dedicated is saturated, can traffic fall back to Hosted automatically?
[05:44] Jordan: Yes — Redwood supports routing policies with automatic fallback to Hosted or to a smaller model variant. There's also cost-aware routing rules to balance latency and expense.
[05:53] Mark: What's the latency impact of that fallback?
[05:56] Priya: Usually negligible if routing is within the same region, maybe +10-40ms depending on model and network. But it's best to simulate during pilot.
[06:05] Alyssa: Ok... (pause) A couple nitty-gritty questions from finance — are we billed for cached tokens? Like if the KV cache hits, do we still pay per-token?
[06:15] Jordan: Great question. Billing depends on how the cache is applied. If the runtime doesn't need to compute the token, it shouldn't charge GPU token compute. But there are some fixed request charges in Hosted. We'll clarify exact billing semantics in the pricing sheet.
[06:30] Mark: Also, what's the minimum contract for Dedicated? We don't want a year-long lock if we don't know adoption.
[06:35] Jordan: We have month-to-month or annual reserved options; the discounts improve on longer commitments. For pilots, many customers do a 1-3 month small reserved pool or start hosted with a plan to convert.
[06:45] Alyssa: Timelines — we want to decide by end of month. Can you turn around the benchmark within a week after we share prompts?
[06:52] Priya: Yes — if you provide an anonymized prompt dump and example SLOs we'll run the benchmark and share results in about 4 business days.
[06:59] Sam: Security-wise, we need SOC2 report, network diagrams, KMS process docs.
[07:04] Jordan: We'll send our SOC2 summary and the security questionnaire. For deeper dives, we can set a session with our Security team — that was one of the next steps.
[07:12] Mark: Competitors — we're also talking to Anthropic and a smaller provider called LatencyCloud. Any quick differentiator?
[07:18] Jordan: Lightweight — Redwood emphasizes production economics and predictable serving across hosted/dedicated/private with built-in routing, KV caching, and Optimize recommendations. Others may offer raw throughput but not the same ops visibility or unified rollout controls.
[07:31] Alyssa: Sounds good. Let's drill into the benchmark plan now.
[07:34] Priya: Plan: you send sample prompts with metadata (avg prompt length, peak concurrency times). We'll pick three model candidates: a baseline production model, a quantized variant, and a smaller cheaper variant. We'll run synthetic concurrency at ratios you see in prod and measure p50/p95/p99, tokens consumed, and cost per useful token. We'll also run a simulated KV cache with varying hit rates (0%, 25%, 50%).
[08:00] Alyssa: For the simulated cache, how do you simulate real-world prefix reuse?
[08:03] Priya: We replay the sequence and identify repeated prefix strings — the same way your assistant composes messages. It's not perfect but gives a solid estimate.
[08:11] Mark: Will the benchmark run in our region? Latency matters.
[08:14] Priya: Yes we'll run regionally to match your EU/US needs. If you require private infra we'll ensure the same cluster sizing in Dedicated.
[08:22] Jordan: Quick check — budget math. If we assume 500k tokens/mo, and caching yields 40% savings with dedicated discount, you can drop unit costs under your target. But we'll put precise numbers in the sheet.
[08:36] Alyssa: If post-benchmark we want to try Dedicated small pool, can Redwood migrate traffic fluidly?
[08:41] Jordan: Yes, rollouts are supported: canary, weighted, automatic fallback. We'll coordinate cutovers.
[08:46] Sam: A practical question: does Redwood provide per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns for us to report to finance?
[08:53] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, token attribution, and cost breakdowns. You can map tokens to teams or routes.
[09:00] Mark: Great. Any gotchas we should watch for?
[09:03] Priya: Watch token inflation in prompts — many teams forget system prompts grow; also pay attention to model context length; longer contexts increase token compute at higher cost. Also be careful with long-running KV caches memory usage; we can set eviction policies.
[09:17] Alyssa: Noted. Ok, let's capture next steps.
[09:20] Jordan: I'll send the pricing sheet and pilot terms by 2027-09-15. Priya will run the benchmark once you share prompts — target results 2027-09-20. We'll also schedule a security deep-dive for week of 2027-09-27.
[09:32] Mark: Sounds good. Anything else?
[09:34] Alyssa: No, that's all for now. Thanks.
[09:36] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the SDK snippets and the questionnaire.
[09:40] (crosstalk as people leave)

Notes: occasional transcription errors: Redwood product names rendered as "Redwood Dedicated" and sometimes "Redwood Dedi" in auto transcript; KMS sometimes mis-typed as K-M-S, PCI spelled correctly but sometimes flagged as P-C-I for clarity.
